answer:
Yes. Source [1] states that semaglutide, a GLP-1 receptor agonist, has shown potential to improve cardiovascular outcomes [1]. Network meta-analyses suggest semaglutide has the highest probability of cardiovascular benefits among GLP-1 receptor agonists, and that semaglutide and albiglutide reduce major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) more than other agents [1].

Source [4] says the FDA has approved semaglutide for reducing major adverse cardiovascular events and heart failure symptoms [4]. Source [5] adds that all forms of semaglutide, oral or injectable, now carry an FDA label stating they may be useful for preventing heart disease [5]. It also reports that even early versions of GLP-1 drugs that did not lead to much weight loss still reduced MACE by around 20% [5].

Overall, the sources provide evidence that GLP-1 drugs such as semaglutide reduce cardiovascular events.
